rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic rent-pricing software or device that pools nonpublic competitor data or sets parallel pricing, and no one may perform such a coordinating function or facilitate parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act. Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic coordinators / parallel pricing coordination in residential rentals
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: takes effect first day of the twelfth month next following enactment (approved 2026-07-20) = 2027-07-01.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act (P.L.1970, c.73); enforcement provisions of sections 6-17 of that Act apply; AG complaint portal.
rules.exemptions: Excludes research/statistical use, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, government affordability controls; inpatient medical, long-term care, and detention facilities are not residential dwelling units.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) prohibits municipal ordinances that conflict with the act, so it may preempt Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic rent ordinances once effective.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any rental residential dwelling unit in the State.
rules.conflict_note: May preempt conflicting local ordinances (e.g., Jersey City § 218-12, Hoboken ch. 158, Art. II) from 2027-07-01; flag for human review.

unverifiable_exemptions: inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention facilities

parsed.doc_summary: NJ P.L.2026, c.43 (FAIR Act), approved 2026-07-20, bans algorithmic rent-coordination software/devices and parallel pricing in residential rentals, effective 2027-07-01, and bars conflicting municipal ordinances.
